one_line: Lion-king of 17th‑century Ladakh, builder of Leh Palace and patron of Drukpa monasteries.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s, athletic but not bulky, with the wiry strength of a high‑altitude rider and climber.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones and a straight nose, warm light‑brown Himalayan complexion, slightly wind‑burned cheeks, sharp dark eyes with a calm, focused gaze; default expression is composed and dignified with a hint of a confident, knowing smile.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered into a high topknot at the crown wrapped with a deep red woolen band, with the rest tied into a single braid falling to mid‑back; no crown, but a simple narrow dark‑brown leather headband under the red wrap, hinting at practical royalty.
appearance.costume: Era‑accurate Ladakhi/Tibetan noble attire: a long maroon woolen chuba (robe) reaching to the ankles, made of thick, slightly textured cloth, crossing left over right and secured with a wide deep‑indigo wool belt; the chuba sleeves are long and slightly flared at the wrists, with dark brown leather facing at the cuffs; over the chest and shoulders he wears a sleeveless dark‑brown sheepskin‑lined vest (bordered with natural off‑white fur at the edges) suggesting travel and leadership in cold highlands; under the chuba, hints of a pale beige linen shirt at the collar; trousers are dark charcoal wool, tucked into sturdy knee‑high brown leather boots with slightly upturned toes and simple stitched patterns; on his left wrist he wears a single copper bracelet, and around his neck a modest mala‑like necklace of dark wooden beads with one small turquoise bead as a quiet nod to his Buddhist devotion and monastic patronage, but no ornate crown or fantasy armor.
appearance.signature: A long, plain but well‑crafted Himalayan iron sword in a dark brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, worn suspended from his belt on the left, hilt wrapped in dark indigo cloth and featuring a simple straight crossguard, symbolizing both royal authority and readiness to defend his kingdom.

ref_desc: Sengge Namgyal is a wiry early‑30s Ladakhi king with an oval, wind‑burned face, dark sharp eyes, black hair in a high red‑wrapped topknot and long braid, wearing a maroon wool chuba, dark brown fur‑edged vest, indigo belt, brown boots, simple wooden‑and‑turquoise mala, and a long indigo‑wrapped‑hilt sword in a brown leather scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of Sengge Namgyal, a dignified 17th‑century Ladakhi king in high Himalayan dress: he is in his early 30s, lean and athletic, with an oval face, warm light‑brown complexion, slightly wind‑burned cheeks and sharp dark eyes, his thick black hair pulled into a high topknot wrapped with a deep red woolen band and the rest tied into a single long braid down his back, with a narrow dark‑brown leather headband beneath. He wears a long maroon wool chuba (Tibetan‑style robe) crossing left over right to the ankles, made of heavy textured cloth, sleeves slightly flared with dark brown leather facing at the cuffs, and a sleeveless dark‑brown sheepskin‑lined vest with off‑white fur edging over his shoulders; a wide deep‑indigo wool belt cinches his waist. Show hints of a pale beige linen shirt at the collar, dark charcoal wool trousers tucked into sturdy knee‑high brown leather boots with simple stitched patterns and slightly upturned toes. Around his neck is a modest wooden mala‑style necklace with one turquoise bead, and on his left wrist a copper bracelet. His signature weapon is a long Himalayan iron sword with a plain straight crossguard, hilt wrapped in deep indigo cloth, carried in a dark brown leather scabbard with simple brass fittings, hanging from his belt on the left. Use a restrained palette of maroon, deep indigo, dark brown, charcoal gray and small turquoise accents, and present him front, side and back in the same outfit so the design is clear and consistent.
